title: The Handshake Stage
logline: When Lily points out that she is Robin's only female friend (Patrice doesn't count), Robin sets out to make another and finds her perfect match: a deadpan Alaskan demolition engineer who counts down before every handshake. Six weeks later the two of them are still stuck at the handshake, locked in a contest over who cares less, while the guys try to prove they have friends outside the group and get exposed one by one.
coldOpen: Kids, your Aunt Robin has always had exactly one best friend. In 2012, Aunt Lily decided that wasn't enough, so Robin went looking for a second. She found her in four days. Getting past the handshake took a little longer.

guests.name: Kit Varga
guests.role: A demolition engineer from Fairbanks, Alaska, who implodes buildings for a living. Flat, procedural and unshakable; counts down out loud before anything risky, handshakes included, treats any feeling as a reason to evacuate the block, and considers Canada 'Alaska's mudroom'

scenes.summary: On the subway to brunch, Lily realizes she is Robin's only female friend (Patrice doesn't count, which relieves Robin). Marshall's two-hundred-hours fact, Robin's 'I don't throw up, I get quieter', Lily's kindergarten Friendship Week chart. Lily's challenge: one new female friend, hugged and brought to the roof party in six weeks. Robin turns it on the guys: Ted's Danish pen pal Klaus is a newsletter; Marshall's Bigfoot buddy Sasquatch Sentinel always reminds him to wear a scarf; Barney's mystery best bro will go anywhere he's told (Ranjit). Everyone brings an outside friend to the roof. Button: the deli lady Robin knows only as 'next'.

beats.line: It started on a Sunday, on the subway to brunch.
Robin, I just realized something horrible. I'm your only female friend.
That's not horrible. That's efficient.
Name one other woman you'd call in an emergency.
Patrice.
Patrice doesn't count.
Oh, thank God.
Robin, there's no shame in it. It takes two hundred hours together to make a close friend. I read that in a dentist's office.
Two hundred hours? I've known my father thirty-three years. We're at maybe nine.
Female friendship is overrated. Two women sit around discussing their feelings. And me. Mostly me.
Robin, what happens when I'm busy? Who do you call when you get dumped? Who holds your hair back?
I'm Canadian, Lily. I don't throw up. I just get quieter.
My kindergarten chart. Every friendship starts at the handshake. My kids get to the hug in about four minutes.
beats.title: Friendship Week: The Five Stages

beats.line: Your kids eat paste.
And some of them have made lifelong friends over that paste.
So here's the deal. One new female friend. Not me, not Patrice. In six weeks, you hug her and bring her to the roof party.
Fine. Six weeks. How hard can it be? I'm extremely likable.
Robin, last month you put a guy in a headlock for saying hi.
He said it weird.
And what about you three? Name one friend you have outside this subway car.
Easy. Klaus. A brilliant Danish architect. We've been corresponding for four years.
Show me.
Dear valued subscriber. This month at Klaus Lindgaard Architects, exciting news about our parking garage.
That's just how Danes open a letter.
Ted, Klaus is a newsletter.
He's a very warm newsletter. I write back every month. He has never once unsubscribed me.
I have an outside friend. Sasquatch Sentinel. We've tracked Bigfoot together online for six years.
Have you ever met him?
He's very private. And very protective. He's always reminding me to wear a scarf.
Baby, have you ever wondered how Sentinel knows your shoe size?
Bigfoot people notice feet, Lily.
Barney?
Please. My best bro outside this group is loyal, discreet, and he'll go anywhere I tell him. You'll meet him on the roof.
Is it Ranjit?
You'll meet him on the roof.
Great. Six weeks, the roof. Everybody brings one outside friend.
Klaus is in Copenhagen.
Klaus is a PDF, Ted.
And Robin? A real friend. A woman you'd actually call.
Fine. I'll start with the deli lady.
You don't know her name.
I know her as next.

scenes.summary: Four days later, Lily takes Robin to a liquor store at eleven p.m. to look for a woman alone buying something sad. Robin and Kit both refuse to admit they want the last bottle of Ben Ardock eighteen. Alaska is Canada's mudroom; forty below is patio weather; Kit implodes buildings and then gets a sandwich. They agree to a Thursday drink, if they're there. Runner 1: Kit counts down to the handshake, then says 'Eh?'. Robin thinks she's the one. Lily buys the abandoned scotch and holds it hostage until somebody hugs Robin: a sticker chart. Montage of six weeks at the handshake stage. Luke calls it two people sitting far apart; Future Ted calls it a whirlwind romance.

beats.line: Four days later, Lily took Robin where her kind of woman shops. A liquor store, at eleven p.m. on a Tuesday.
Okay. Look for a woman alone, at night, buying something sad.
Lily. I am a woman alone, at night, buying something sad.
Exactly. Look for you.
Last bottle of Ben Ardock eighteen. It's a sign.
You taking that?
Wasn't planning on it.
Me neither.
Then take it.
Don't want it. Wanting things is how they get you.
I've got four at home anyway.
One's for guests?
I don't have guests.
Respect.
She's you! She's you in flannel! Ask where she's from!
Where are you from?
Fairbanks, Alaska. You?
Vancouver.
Oh. Canada. Alaska's mudroom.
Excuse me?
It's where we leave our boots.
We get forty below in Canada.
We call that patio weather.
Lily. I want to punch her. In a good way.
What do you do?
Demolition. I implode buildings. Kit Varga.
Robin Scherbatsky. Anything I'd know?
The Hotel Marquette. Last spring.
My friend Ted cried for a week over that building.
Everybody cries. Then I go get a sandwich.
Ask her to hang out!
Want to grab a drink sometime? Or not. I don't care.
Thursday. McGee's. Seven. If I'm there, I'm there.
And if I'm not, I'm not.
Then we understand each other. Handshake. On three.
Three. Two. One.
Did you just count down to a handshake?
I count down to everything. Occupational.
Good grip.
Not bad for a Canadian.
Eh?
Robin! You made a friend!
She insulted my country, my handshake and my vowels. Lily, I think she's the one.
She left the scotch.
So did I. If I take it, she knows I wanted it.
One sad bottle, please. You get it back the day somebody hugs you.
That's extortion.
It's a sticker chart.
So.
So.
Good talk.
Best one yet.
Handshake. On three.
Let's not rush things.
Dad. That whole montage was two people sitting really far apart.
Luke, for Aunt Robin, that was a whirlwind romance.

scenes.summary: The night of the roof party, at Luigi's. Lily and Marshall spy from the next table ('Talk about something boring.' 'So my friend Sentinel says...'). Robin hid in the coat check to arrive later than Kit; Kit has been in the walk-in freezer since five fifteen. They compete over who knows less about the other. Sasquatch Sentinel texts Marshall: bowling with your father, wear a scarf, love, Mom. Runner 2: a controlled hug, on five, aborted at three ('Never trust a building'). Robin lets slip that her anchor slot went to a skateboarding bulldog; Kit would have to evacuate the block, and Lily is hurt she wasn't told. Kit's best friend of eleven years arrives: Patrice, who hugs her with no countdown. Patrice won Kit with eleven months of cookies at her door. Patrice counts. Button: Marshall heard everything, and his mom is Bigfoot.

beats.line: Six weeks later, on the night of the roof party, Robin had one last dinner to get to the hug. Lily came to observe.
Six weeks, Marshall. Six Thursdays. They've never even sat on the same side of a table.
Baby, she'll see us. We're four feet from her table, and I'm six foot four.
She'll see a boring couple on a date. Act natural. Say something boring.
Okay. So my friend Sentinel says—
Perfect.
Sorry I'm late.
Just got here.
I got here at six thirty. I waited in the coat check for an hour so I'd be later than you.
Five fifteen. Walk-in freezer.
Respect.
I didn't read the menu. I'll eat whatever.
I didn't read the sign outside. I don't know where we are.
I don't know what you do on weekends.
I don't know your middle name.
I don't have one.
Didn't ask.
This isn't a friendship. It's a hostage exchange.
Ooh, Sentinel texted me back about the roof party!
Can't. Bowling with your father. Wear a scarf, sweetie. Love, Mom. I mean, Sentinel.
beats.title: Sasquatch Sentinel

messages.text: Roof party tonight! Finally meet in person?
Wear a scarf, sweetie. Love, Mom.

beats.line: Lily. Sasquatch Sentinel is my mother.
Baby, I've known for six years. She signs every post, love, Mom.
I told that man things, Lily. About Bigfoot. About our honeymoon.
Scherbatsky. Proposal. We attempt a hug. Controlled. On five.
Copy.
Five. Four. Three.
Abort.
Too much wind.
We're indoors.
Never trust a building.
Since neither of us cares. Today they gave my anchor slot to a bulldog on a skateboard.
Are you about to have a feeling?
No.
Good. If you have a feeling, I have to evacuate the block.
She didn't tell me about the bulldog.
She will, baby. She always ends up telling you.
I have to go. My best friend's picking me up.
You have a best friend?
Eleven years. Against my will.
Kitty Cat!
Patrice?
Robin! You know Kitty? Oh my gosh, BFF fun day for three!
Nobody asked you, Patrice!
I made you a muffin anyway!
How? How did she get past the handshake?
She lived across the hall when I moved here. Left cookies at my door every night.
And you opened it?
Month eleven.
Best thing that ever happened to me. Don't tell her.
She tells me every Christmas!
Scherbatsky. Next Thursday. If I'm there, I'm there.
Patrice counts.
How much of that did you two hear?
Nothing.
Everything. Also, my mom is Bigfoot.

scenes.summary: The roof party. Klaus finally replies, with an out-of-office. Barney's best bro outside the group is Ranjit: the friendship is free, the stairs are forty dollars. Marshall's mother was tracking him, not Bigfoot. Robin arrives alone; Kit is at BFF fun day with Patrice. Marshall clears the roof for wings (extra). Lily apologizes; she heard about the bulldog through a woman who lives in a freezer. Robin came up here because she knew Lily would follow: everyone else she keeps at the handshake, but Lily hugged her the night they met with no countdown. Lily brought the sad bottle, a third gone. Runner 3: Robin counts down to a hug, and Lily hugs her at two. Undercut: Lily is Robin's Patrice. Future Ted: Robin and Kit have never hugged (they got to two in 2019), and Lily has never once let Robin get to one.

beats.line: Klaus replied! For the first time in four years!
And?
It's an out-of-office. He's in Aarhus until the fourteenth.
He's never told me where he was before. We're getting closer.
Ted. You're pen pals with a mailing list. Prepare to meet my best bro outside the group.
Hello!
That's Ranjit.
Ranjit has seen me cry in the back of a limo twice. Both times about a suit. That's friendship.
Ranjit. Tell Ted what we are.
Best friends! And on Fridays it is time and a half.
We said the friendship was off the meter.
It is! The friendship is free. The stairs are forty dollars.
My outside friend can't make it. She's bowling with my dad.
Your mom spent six years hunting Bigfoot with you? That is the most Minnesota thing I've ever heard.
She wasn't hunting Bigfoot, Barney. She was tracking me.
Robin! Where's your friend?
She's at a BFF fun day. With Patrice.
Patrice has a best friend?
Patrice has a best friend. I have a woman I shake hands with on Thursdays.
Guys. Wings. Right now.
But it's the roof party.
Ted. There are wings.
Wings are extra!
Robin, I'm sorry. I pushed you into this.
You were right. I have exactly one female friend.
Who found out about the bulldog through a woman who lives in a freezer.
I didn't tell you because you'd make me talk about it.
I would have.
I know. That's why I came up here.
I knew you'd follow me.
Everyone I've ever met, I keep at the handshake. Not you. You hugged me the night we met. No countdown. Nothing.
You went stiff as a board.
I still do. I just stopped telling you.
I brought the sad bottle. Sticker chart's full.
You kept it for six weeks?
I drank about a third. It's been a long six weeks.
Okay. Hug. On three. Three. Two—
Too slow, Scherbatsky.
Oh no. Lily. You're my Patrice.
Take that back.
You barge in. You never leave. I bet you have a muffin.
I will push you off this roof.
There she is.
Kids, Robin and Kit are still friends. Nineteen years of Thursdays. They have never once hugged. In 2019, they got all the way to two.
And your Aunt Lily? In all those years, she has never once let Robin get to one.
